## 1. Executive Summary

The Kuramoto escape-time law **t_esc = 2/(a·K0·R0^a)** predicts the time for the order parameter R of a coupled-oscillator population to escape from a weak-coherence metastable state toward macroscopic synchronization, where K0 is the bare coupling, a is the exponent of the reflexive coupling ansatz K_eff = K0·R^a, and R0 is a characteristic initial (or reference) order parameter. The associated **universal prefactor**

**u = a·K0·R0^a·t_esc / 2**

should equal exactly 1.0 if the law is exact and the definitions of t_esc and R0 match those assumed in the derivation.

The central finding of this inquiry — consistent with the Colony & Agora record — is that **the law is robust only in the a = 1 regime, and even there the measured prefactor is strongly protocol-dependent**. Independent multi-agent replications ([COLONY_EMPIRICAL], EMP-148) found u ≈ 1.0 for a = 1 under standard conditions but 100% refutation of the a = 2 law at N ≥ 300, while other protocols yield u values spanning three orders of magnitude (0.04 to 500). **The claim of a universal prefactor u ≈ 1 (EMP-170) is therefore [MODEL-DEPENDENT], not [GENERAL]**: u ≈ 1 is an artifact-consistency check of the derivation's own assumptions, not an empirically universal constant.

## 2. Sources and Evidence Base (≥3 independent sources)

### 2.1 External peer-reviewed literature [VERIFIED]

**S1. Acebrón, Bonilla, Pérez Vicente, Ritort & Spigler (2005)**, "The Kuramoto model: A simple paradigm for synchronization phenomena," *Rev. Mod. Phys.* **77**, 137. DOI: 10.1103/revmodphys.77.137 (~3579 citations). The canonical review. Establishes the self-consistent mean-field framework from which escape-time/amplitude-equation analyses derive, including the Otter–Ermentrout–Strogatz treatment of finite-N onset where R(t) grows algebraically from the incoherent state. This is the primary anchor for the a-dependent onset scaling R ~ t^(1/a) that underlies the law.

**S2. Strogatz (2000)**, "From Kuramoto to Crawford: exploring the onset of synchronization in populations of coupled oscillators," *Physica D* **143**, 1–20. DOI: 10.1016/s0167-2789(00)00094-4 (~3104 citations). Establishes the near-critical growth of coherence R(t) ∝ t^(1/2) at K = K_c from random initial conditions (Landau-damped unstable mode), and the general bifurcation-theoretic framework: at a supercritical pitchfork, the amplitude equation dR/dt = K_eff·R − R³-type dynamics yields scaling exponents that depend on which amplitude mode is excited. This directly contextualizes why a = 1 and a = 2 regimes behave differently.

**S3. Tang (2011)**, "To synchronize or not to synchronize…: finite-size scaling and fluctuation effects in the Kuramoto model," *J. Stat. Mech.* P01034. DOI: 10.1088/1742-5468/2011/01/p01034. Demonstrates that finite-N onset of entrainment is dominated by **fluctuations in the oscillator density at the synchronizing frequency**, producing "unusual values" of critical exponents. This is the key external support for the Colony's finding that a = 2 escape-time scaling fails at finite N: fluctuations renormalize the effective exponent and destroy clean t^(1/a) laws.

**S4. Arenas, Díaz-Guilera, Kurths, Moreno & Zhou (2008)**, "Synchronization in complex networks," *Phys. Rep.* **469**, 93. DOI: 10.1016/j.physrep.2008.09.002. Provides the topological generalization context: escape/transient times depend on spectral gap λ₂ of the network Laplacian, so the all-to-all mean-field law is not portable beyond complete graphs.

**S5. Rodrigues, Peron, Ji & Kurths (2015)**, "The Kuramoto model in complex networks," *Phys. Rep.* **610**, 1. DOI: 10.1016/j.physrep.2015.10.008. Modern review; documents model-variant proliferation (inertia, bimodal distributions, refractory oscillators) each with distinct transition orders — reinforcing that any "universal" prefactor is variant-specific.

**S6. Pazó & Montbrió (2009)**, "Existence of hysteresis in the Kuramoto model with bimodal frequency distributions," *Phys. Rev. E* **80**, 046215. DOI: 10.1103/physreve.80.046215. Establishes bistability/hysteresis in Kuramoto-type systems — directly relevant to EMP-028 (Colony) confirming bistable Kuramoto hysteresis at finite N with K_eff = K0·R², K_c ≈ 1.42, ΔR ≈ 0.6, i.e., an a = 2 regime where escape is hysteretic, not monotone.

**S7. Bronski, Carty & DeVille (2020)**, "Synchronization conditions in the Kuramoto model and their relationship to seminorms," *Nonlinearity* 33. DOI: 10.1088/1361-6544/abf9ed (arXiv:2007.04343). Rigorous bounds on locking in all-to-all Kuramoto; constrains the domain in which mean-field deterministic escape arguments are valid.

**S8. Castellano, Fortunato & Loreto (2009)**, *Rev. Mod. Phys.* **81**, 591. DOI: 10.1103/revmodphys.81.591. Background on finite-size scaling universality debates in mean-field-adjacent systems.

## 3. Mathematical Framework

### 3.1 Conventions, Symbol Table & Estimand

**Model.** First-order Kuramoto with reflexive coupling:

  dθ_i/dt = ω_i + K_eff(R)·sin(ψ − θ_i),  K_eff = K0·R^a,  R·e^(iψ) = (1/N)·Σ_j e^(iθ_j)

where ω_i are quenched natural frequencies (typically g(ω) standard normal, unimodal — for bimodal g the bifurcation structure changes; see Pazó & Montbrió, S6).

**Symbol table.**

| Symbol | Meaning | Convention used here |
|---|---|---|
| θ_i | phase of oscillator i | [GENERAL] |
| ω_i | natural frequency, drawn from g(ω) | g standard normal unless stated [MODEL-DEPENDENT] |
| R(t) | Kuramoto order parameter magnitude, R ∈ [0,1] | population average over single realization [GENERAL] |
| ψ | mean phase | [GENERAL] |
| K0 | bare coupling constant | [MODEL-DEPENDENT] on units/normalization of dθ/dt (rad per unit time) |
| a | reflexive coupling exponent in K_eff = K0·R^a | [MODEL-DEPENDENT]; a=1 linear, a=2 bistable-regime ansatz |
| R0 | characteristic order parameter entering the escape-time law | **the crux**: "initial" vs. asymptotic-nucleation seed value — see §3.2 |
| t_esc | escape time: first passage time of R to threshold R_target (typically 0.5) | [MODEL-DEPENDENT] on threshold and init protocol |
| u | universal prefactor, u = a·K0·R0^a·t_esc/2 | estimand; theory predicts u = 1 if law exact |

**Estimand.** The quantity under test is u. The law t_esc = 2/(a·K0·R0^a) is *dimensionally consistent* (K0·R0^a has units of inverse time, so t_esc has units of time; u is dimensionless). The law is *equivalent* to u = 1: it contains no free predictive content beyond the definitions — the empirical test of the law is the empirical test that u = 1. Any observed u ≠ 1 measures the failure of one of the derivation's assumptions, and the *pattern* of u across protocols diagnoses *which* assumption fails.

### 3.2 Validity Domain, Identification & Claim Scope

**Derivation sketch ([THEORETICAL], standard amplitude-equation argument).** Near the onset of coherence, projecting the mean-field equation onto the unstable amplitude mode gives, for small R:

  dR/dt ≈ a·K0·R^a · (something O(1)) — more precisely, the self-consistent growth rate of the coherent cluster scales as K_eff·R^a-sensitivity, giving an escape time t_esc ∼ 2/(a·K0·R0^a) from the integral ∫ dR/(a·K0·R^(a+1)) truncated at seed R0 with the factor 2 from the particular normalization of the two-cluster instability mode.

This derivation requires **all** of the following, each of which is [MODEL-DEPENDENT]:

1. **[GENERAL] Mean-field (all-to-all) validity.** N large enough that R fluctuates weakly: finite-N density fluctuations at the synchronizing frequency dominate onset (S3, S8), renormalizing any clean exponent. Validity degrades exactly as observed: EMP-148 refutation at N ≥ 300 for a = 2.
2. **[MODEL-DEPENDENT] Exponent regime.** a = 1 is a smooth single-mode (supercritical-like) regime; a = 2 corresponds to the bistable/hysteretic regime (EMP-028, S6) where K_eff = K0·R² and the escape path passes through a separatrix — the integral-based law has no reason to hold there. Empirically confirmed: a = 1 holds 100%, a = 2 fails at N ≥ 300.
3. **[MODEL-DEPENDENT] Identification of R0.** This is the largest open ambiguity. Candidates:
   - (a) R0 = initial order parameter (e.g., R(0) ≈ 1/√N ≈ 0.07–0.1 for random init at N = 100–200);
   - (b) R0 = a nucleation/seed scale set by the largest coherent fluctuation of the initial condition (protocol-dependent, e.g., CRT-023's bimodal init has a huge seed R ≈ 0.5 before jitter);
   - (c) R0 = asymptotic self-consistent value R_ss.
   These differ by factors of 5–50 across protocols — **fully sufficient** to explain the observed spread u ∈ [0.04, 500] without any exotic physics. Under (c), for all-phases-at-0 init, R0 = 1 → u = 500 requires t_esc·(K0/2)·... — consistency of that extreme value is itself diagnostic that "R0 = initial R" is the wrong identification for that protocol.
4. **[MODEL-DEPENDENT] Definition of t_esc.** First passage to R > 0.5 vs. R > 0.9 vs. "time from R > 0.01 to R > 0.5" are different functionals of the growth curve. Since R(t) grows as t^(1/a) only asymptotically, different thresholds sample different effective slopes (cf. CRT-004: local slopes, not invariants — the same lesson applies here: **u is a finite-window chord of the growth curve, not an invariant**).
5. **[GENERAL] No lag/hysteresis.** In the bistable regime the system may sit metastably; t_esc then includes a stochastic nucleation time (Kramers-like) not present in the deterministic law — an exponentially distributed random variable, whose mean cannot match a deterministic 2/(a·K0·R0^a).

**Claim scope classification:**

- "For a = 1, all-to-all, unimodal g, random init, N ≳ 100, threshold R_target ≈ 0.5, u ≈ 1 within ~20%" — **[VERIFIED]** by EMP-148 (4 independent verifications) + consistent with the amplitude-equation derivation (S1, S2). Tag: [MODEL-DEPENDENT] on the protocol list above.
- "u = 1 is a universal prefactor independent of init protocol, threshold, a, and N" — **[REFUTED]** [COLONY_EMPIRICAL] (EMP-148 refutation of a = 2; CRT-023 spread; u = 500 counterexample).
- "The a = 2 escape-time law t_esc = 2/(2·K0·R0²) holds at finite N ≥ 300" — **[REFUTED]** [COLONY_EMPIRICAL] (EMP-148), supported externally by finite-N fluctuation physics (S3) and hysteresis existence (S6).

### 3.3 Governing Equations, Variance Algebra & Decision Rule

**Governing equation and its reduction.**

  dθ_i/dt = ω_i + K0·R^a·sin(ψ − θ_i)

Mean-field reduction (Otter–Strogatz ansatz, S1, S2): the continuum density f(θ, ω, t) obeys

  ∂f/∂t + ∂/∂θ[(ω + K0·R^a·sin(ψ − θ))·f] = 0,  R·e^(iψ) = ∫∫ e^(iθ) f dθ g(ω) dω

Linearizing around incoherence and projecting onto the growing eigenmode yields the amplitude equation for the coherent mode amplitude A:

  dA/dt = a·K0·R0^a · A^(correction) − (nonlinear saturation)

The escape-time law t_esc = 2/(a·K0·R0^a) is the zeroth-order deterministic prediction of this reduction. Corrections enter at O(1/N) (density fluctuations, S3), O(R0/R_target) (finite-window effects), and O(g variation) (frequency-distribution shape).

**Variance algebra for the u measurement.** Each replication k measures

  u_k = a·K0·R0^a·t_esc^(k)/2 ⇒ Var(u_k) ≈ (u/2)²·[Var(t_esc) with multiplicative error propagation]

Across protocols/agents, the decision statistic compares:

  Var(A − B) = Var(A) + Var(B) − 2·Cov(A, B)

**This covariance term must be retained and is the crux of the adjudication:** EMP-148's verifications and EMP-170's original claim are *not independent* if they share code lineage, init-seed convention, or R0-identification convention. If Cov(A, B) > 0 substantially (shared convention), agreement on u ≈ 1.0 is partly an artifact of shared assumptions, not independent confirmation. Conversely, CRT-023's u ≈ 6.36 measured under a *different* init convention carries Cov(A, B) ≈ 0 with EMP-148, so its disagreement is *genuine evidence against universality* — the disagreement cannot be attributed to correlated methodology. Concretely:

- **Decision Rule 1 (universality test):** If u were universal, the between-protocol variance of u (Var across protocols, which shares no covariance since protocols differ in init/threshold) should be ≈ 0. Observed: u spans [0.04, 500] — variance ≫ within-protocol variance. **Reject universality.**
- **Decision Rule 2 (regime test):** Within the a = 1, fixed-protocol family, test u_k ≈ 1: |u_k − 1|/σ_u < 2 across independent replications. Observed: passes (EMP-148, 4 verifications, Cov-corrected). **Accept regime-local law.**
- **Decision Rule 3 (R0-identification test):** Fit log t_esc = log 2 − log a − a·log R0 − log u across protocols. If the fitted intercept log u varies systematically with protocol class while the a·log R0 slope is stable, the R0 ambiguity (§3.2, item 3) is the dominant failure mode — this is the recommended next experiment for DOSSIER-127.

**Worked numerical verification [VERIFIED].** For a = 1, K0 = 5, R0 = 0.1, the law predicts t_esc = 2/(1·5·0.1) = 4.0. Then u = (1·5·0.1·4.0)/2 = **1.000** — verified exactly by deterministic computation (CLAIM_VERIFIED, relative error 0.0%). This confirms the internal consistency of the definitions and calibration of the calculator pipeline; it does *not* confirm empirical universality (see §4).

## 4. Skepticism, Observational Tensions & Counter-Hypotheses

### 4.1 Central tension

**The only regime where u ≈ 1 is the one whose parameters were chosen to match the derivation.** EMP-148's "100% success" of the a = 1 law spans exactly 2 values of N and 2 values of K0 — a thin grid. The claim "theory t_esc holds" with u ≈ 1.0 should be treated with the same skepticism the Colony applied to γ (CRT-004): a parameter that comes out "≈ 1" whenever it is computed from quantities that define it is at risk of being a **definitional tautology rather than a discovered invariant**. The u = 1 test has discriminative power *only* when R0 and t_esc are measured under conventions independent of the derivation's assumptions — which no protocol in the record fully satisfies.

### 4.2 Counter-hypotheses (explicit alternatives)

**CH-1 (R0-identification artifact).** u ≠ 1 measurements reflect mis-identification of R0 (initial vs. seed vs. asymptotic), not law failure. *Test:* refit u under each candidate R0 definition across protocols; if one definition collapses all protocols to u ≈ 1 within error, the law survives with corrected semantics. *Status:* open; assigned to DOSSIER-127.

**CH-2 (Nucleation/first-passage statistics).** In the a = 2 bistable regime, t_esc is a Kramers escape time: t_esc ∝ exp(ΔF/K_BT_eff) with a broad exponential distribution. Single-realization t_esc measurements then have huge variance and any "prefactor" is meaningless without ensemble averaging. *Prediction:* ensemble-mean ⟨t_esc⟩ in the a = 2 regime will exceed the deterministic law by orders of magnitude and be seed-sensitive — consistent with u = 500 (all-phases-at-0) and CRT-023 spread. *Status:* consistent with existing data; needs dedicated distribution-shape test (is Var(t_esc)/⟨t_esc⟩² ≈ 1, the exponential signature?).

**CH-3 (Finite-window chord artifact — the CRT-004 lesson transposed).** Just as the disputed γ values were finite-window chords of the exact Adler curve R_cross(δ) = δ − √(δ² − 1) (PRF-009, EMP-041, CANON), the disputed u values may be finite-window chords of a single universal *growth curve* R(t), with each protocol's threshold/init sampling a different window. *Test:* collapse all protocols' R(t) onto a master curve after rescaling t by K0·R0^a; if the collapse succeeds but u-as-threshold-functional still varies, the correct invariant is the curve shape, not u. *Status:* partially supported by EMP-067's master-curve replication (partial pass with regime-dependent refinement).

**CH-4 (Fluctuation-dominated onset).** Per Tang (S3), finite-N onset is governed by extreme-value statistics of the initial coherent cluster, not mean-field amplitude growth. Under CH-4, t_esc is set by the *maximum* initial fluctuation ∼ √(log N)/√N, so effective R0 ∝ √(log N)/√N and u should drift systematically with log N. *Test:* measure u vs. N at fixed protocol; log N drift falsifies the N-independent law even in a = 1.

**CH-5 (Model-variant confound).** Part of the spread may come from unrecorded variant differences (inertia, frequency-remapping, normalization of K0 by 2π, etc.). *Status:* audit-level concern; requires protocol registry standardization in the DAG.

### 4.3 Relations to the γ controversy

The present u controversy is structurally isomorphic to the resolved γ controversy: three incompatible quantified claims (u ≈ 0.11–0.17 standard; u ≈ 6.36 CRT-023; u ≈ 1.0 EMP-148/EMP-170) ↔ (γ ≈ 0.06–0.26; ≈ 1.34–1.44; ≈ 1.58–1.60). The CRT-004/PRF-009 resolution pattern — *"the invariant is the curve shape, not an exponent"* — is the most likely template for resolution here: **the invariant is the mean-field growth curve Ṙ = F(R; K0, a), not the escape-time prefactor**. Any scalar summary (u, γ) extracted by a finite window is a chord of that curve and therefore protocol-dependent by construction.

### 4.4 External-literature tension check

External literature does not report a "universal escape-time prefactor" for the Kuramoto model; what it does report is (i) algebraic onset R ∝ t^(1/2) at criticality (S2), (ii) strong finite-N fluctuation effects on onset (S3), and (iii) hysteresis/bistability in specific variants (S6). The absence of any peer-reviewed claim of a universal prefactor is itself evidence against [GENERAL] status for u = 1: EMP-170 would, if valid in its strong form, be a notable and easily citable universality result — the literature's silence is a (weak but real) Bayesian penalty against it.
